abstract: Vehicle routing with heterogeneous vehicle speeds remains a core challenge in logistics. We propose a low-latency-Vehicle-First Sweep (FVFS) heuristic that sorts customers by polar angle, orders vehicles by descending speed, and greedily assigns customers while respecting capacity. FVFS preserves a strict prefix invariant that guarantees feasibility and yields a makespan within a constant factor of the optimal for the considered speed model. We provide a formal proof of invariant preservation and analyze the algorithm's asymptotic complexity. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 single-core PHP runtime shows a mean latency of 42 043 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 23 785 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261009_050221_improved_approximations_for_ve}
